newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - July 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - July 9.

text.p: These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday.
The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- MING PAO said it understood the dilemma the new government faced with illegal immigrant children from China but said it could not support the bill which would send them back because it violated the Basic Law, Hong Kong's post-handover constitution. The paper said it could not support the government in openly depriving Hong Kong citizens of their right of abode.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES supported the government's decision to send back mainland children all at once, saying it would have a huge impact on the territory's public order and social stability. The paper urged the government to take action immediately.

-- TA KUNG PAO said the bill was in line with the spirit of the Basic Law and could stop more illegal immigrants from sneaking into the territory. The paper urged the Provisional Legislature to cooperate with the government in an effort to crack down on illegal immigration.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL said new election rules announced by the government were generally acceptable. It was a wise decision not to include mainland companies in the functional constituencies, but it criticised the government for excluding the higher education sector. While the government is talking about raising education levels and developing high technology, it puts the political status of missile experts far below that of food hawkers, the paper said.
